pages.text: Tough As Nails tracks your $(bold)temperature$(): five bands, Icy, Cold, Neutral, Warm, Hot. The gauge is by your hotbar. Winter nights, snow, deep water and altitude pull it down; deserts, the Nether and summer noon push it up.$(br2)Thirst is $(bold)off$(). Temperature is the survival layer.

$(bold)Icy$() and $(bold)Hot$() hurt you over time. $(bold)Cold$() and $(bold)Warm$() are warnings. The shift takes a while, so you can cross a cold valley; you cannot camp in it unprepared.$(br2)Heat sources (campfires, torches, lava, furnaces) warm the air nearby; water, ice and shade cool it.
Wool warms, leaves cool. Every two pieces move you one band toward Neutral; armor never pushes you into Hot or Icy.
Leaf armor for deserts and the Nether. Both sets are cheap and always craftable; they are the basic climate clothing and they are free.
A thermometer reads the air where you stand; a temperature gauge is a block that reads a room. Build one before you build a greenhouse.

The thermoregulator is a block that heats or cools a room, fed with fuel or ice. Fans and air conditioners (TAN+) go further. These are $(bold)advanced climate control$() and are part of the Blueprint ladder; wool and leaves never are.
pages.title: Advanced climate control

pages.text: $(bold)Thermal Tuning$() is an armor enchantment that holds you at Neutral. Rare, and worth a slot.$(br2)Plan the first winter: a roof, a fire, wool, and food that gives Comfort. Plan the first summer: shade and water near the fields.
